title: Connect to Papyrus MCP through normal sign-in with a fixed session deadline
description:
As a signed-in Papyrus editor or reader, I want to connect an agent with the site's normal sign-in and one consent, so that it can act with my permissions for a bounded period.

This story is the behavior contract for PPY-9bf332 and the live gate in PPY-17c201. Existing tools and cards from draft PR #1244 are the baseline. Keep the endpoint site-bound and authenticated, and keep public browsing on ordinary HTTP. An MCP connection records the verified person and the agent channel. Existing human-only delegation and publication gates still decide who can approve those actions. An authorized Reference decision can be made through a tool call or its card.

```gherkin
Feature: Connect an agent to a Papyrus publication

  Scenario: A signed-out editor connects
    Given the editor starts an MCP connection for a publication
    When the editor completes the site's normal Google sign-in
    Then the same browser flow shows the registered client, publication and verified staff identity
    And one approval returns the editor to the host with access as that identity

  Scenario: A reader connects on a same-origin publication
    Given Reader Steering allows signed-in readers to submit links
    When the reader completes Prospectus sign-in and approves the connection
    Then a submission is attributed to that site's reader subject
    And the connection cannot discover or use private editorial tools

  Scenario: A staff connection renews within its approved time
    Given the publication approved renewable staff access
    When the host refreshes after the original access token expires
    Then only the replacement refresh token can renew the connection
    And the connection ends by seven days after approval or earlier upstream expiry
    And connecting again after expiry requires a fresh sign-in and approval

  Scenario: The owner disconnects one client
    Given the editor has two connections to a publication
    When the editor disconnects one connection
    Then its access and refresh tokens fail on the next use
    And the other connection is still usable

  Scenario: The host reconnects after a server restart
    Given an installed plugin uses the publication's stable HTTPS MCP URL
    When the service restarts and the host refreshes its connection
    Then the host can use the same installation
    And the host needs no manually provisioned keys or AWS credentials
```

Record separately whether discovery, sign-in, refresh, tools and optional cards work in the real host. A synthetic provider or intercepted callback is a preflight result.
